_comment: Copy to watch_rules.json next to server.py and edit. The real file is gitignored. Everything a rule does not set is taken from 'defaults', so a working rule is three or four lines. Placeholders are ${name}; an unknown one is left in the text as-is, so a typo is visible instead of silently empty. An UPPERCASE $NAME in url, headers, proxy or body is expanded from the environment (.env) when the file is loaded - keep tokens, chat ids and proxy passwords there, not here. If every receiver needs the same proxy, move it into 'defaults'; if some receivers are on the LAN, keep it per rule.

rules._comment: Remote access into the home network. Unlike a web-configurator login, which KeeneticOS 5.1.1 does not log at all, this event carries the user, the source IP and the address handed out.
rules.message: VPN-подключение к домашней сети: ${m2} (${m1}) с адреса ${m3}

rules._comment: The only trace someone who knows the admin password leaves behind: settings were saved. Fires on this server's own write tools too - they save the same way and the log does not say who asked.
rules.message: На роутере сохранена конфигурация (веб-конфигуратор или RCI)
Незнакомое устройство в сети: ${mac}, IP ${ip}, имя '${name}', hostname '${hostname}', сеть ${interface_name}

rules._comment: Straight to the Telegram Bot API instead of a webhook. api.telegram.org is unreachable directly from this router, so it goes through the same proxy Home Assistant uses. Put all three in .env: TG_TOKEN, TG_CHAT_ID and TG_PROXY=http://user:pass@host:port - the proxy demands authentication (a bare CONNECT gets 407). Only UPPERCASE names are read from the environment. Enable this or the webhook rule, not both.
rules.message: VPN-подключение к домашней сети: ${m2} (${m1}) с адреса ${m3}
